summary: Blackboard Manager component designed with 6 work packages covering core data structure, read/write operations, session management, event system, persistence, and API interfaces.

work_packages.title: Core Blackboard Data Structure
work_packages.description: Design and implement the core blackboard data structure that serves as the shared knowledge base for all agents. This includes defining the schema for blackboard entries, implementing thread-safe storage mechanisms, and establishing the fundamental data model for key-value pairs with metadata.

work_packages.title: Read/Write Operations with Concurrency Control
work_packages.description: Implement thread-safe read and write operations for the blackboard. This includes atomic read operations, atomic write operations, compare-and-swap for concurrent updates, and proper locking mechanisms to prevent race conditions when multiple agents access the blackboard simultaneously.

work_packages.title: Session Management
work_packages.description: Implement session management for the blackboard, including creating new sessions, listing active sessions, retrieving session history, and managing session lifecycle. Each session represents a conversation or task context with its own blackboard state.

work_packages.title: Event and Notification System
work_packages.description: Design and implement an event-driven notification system that allows agents to subscribe to blackboard changes. This includes publishing events when entries are created/updated/deleted, subscription management for agents, and event filtering based on topics or patterns.

work_packages.title: Persistence and Recovery
work_packages.description: Implement persistence mechanisms for the blackboard data, including saving blackboard state to disk, loading state on startup, implementing backup and recovery procedures, and ensuring data durability across system restarts.

work_packages.title: Agent API Interface
work_packages.description: Design and implement the public API interface that agents use to interact with the blackboard. This includes methods for reading entries, writing entries, subscribing to changes, querying blackboard state, and managing agent-specific views or namespaces within the blackboard.
